tasks.short: Examine finished pieces for chipped edges and marred surfaces, sort defective pieces by flaw, count rejects per flaw and tell the setter about repeated flaws.

steps.what: Press operator examines completed workpieces for chipped edges or marred surfaces
Press operator sorts defective pieces according to types of flaws
Press operator marks each reject by flaw type: a mark on the shift sheet today, a flaw button on the terminal after the change
Press operator adds up the rejects per flaw type at shift end: by hand today, counted by the terminal after the change
Press operator tells the setter about repeated flaws

tasks.design: The machine terminal ({OPS_SYSTEM}) has a button per flaw type, so the operator presses a button for each reject instead of a mark on paper, and the terminal adds up the counts instead of the operator at shift end. Counts are shown per machine and shift, not per operator. Examining, sorting and talking to the setter stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rejects were tallied with marks on a paper sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Machine terminals take reason codes for scrap and show counts per shift.
tasks.still_hard: New flaw types need a new code before they can be counted.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling a burr that is hard to see.

reach.learn: Whether flaw counts point to tool wear sooner.

evidence.claim: Machine terminals take reason codes for scrap and show counts per shift.
Machine data tied to an operator login can observe performance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from finished pieces to the setter informed; rework is outside.
Input contract: flaw types set by the quality inspector; fallback is the paper sheet.
Examining, sorting, marking each reject and telling the setter keep their full time; a button press is no faster than a mark. Only adding up the marks (s3b) goes.
Counts are kept per machine and shift.

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep for the operator: the button presses are in s3, and flaw codes are set by the quality inspector.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new flaw types without a code and older terminals leave half of the rejects on the paper sheet, so half of the adding up stays (2.0); high: all flaw types have a button (4.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Fetch the work order and drawing, read specifications, check the drawing revision, find the material and ask about unclear specifications.

steps.what: Press operator fetches the paper work order and drawing from the office: every job today; after the change only for drawings not yet released on the terminal
Press operator reads work orders to determine specifications such as materials, cutting lines and tolerances
Press operator checks that the drawing revision is current
Press operator asks the planner or engineer about unclear specifications
Press operator looks up material certificates and stock location

tasks.design: The machine terminal ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows the next work order from the schedule with the released drawing revision and the material's certificate and stock location from the ERP ({ERP}). Reading specifications and asking about unclear ones stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper work orders and drawings were fetched from the office, and old revisions sometimes reached the floor.
tasks.enabler_now: Shop-floor terminals show work orders and released drawings from the ERP.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear or incomplete drawings still need the engineer.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a tolerance that the material cannot hold.

reach.learn: Whether digital release cuts wrong-revision jobs.

evidence.claim: Shop-floor terminals show work orders and released drawings from the ERP.
Operator logins on terminals can observe attendance and performance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the schedule to located material; setting up the machine is outside.
Input contract: work orders released by the planner; drawings released by engineering; fallback is paper.

Reading and asking keep their full time. s1 keeps 10 for drawings that are still only on paper; s3 goes because the terminal shows only the released revision; s5 keeps 40 for reading the certificate and location on screen.
Engineers' time is outside the operator's savings.

incremental.description: Press operator logs in and confirms the job on the terminal.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: engineering releases only half of the drawings to the terminal, so half of the jobs are still fetched and checked on paper (20.0); high: work orders and drawings released as assumed (33.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Start the machine and run first pieces, monitor and adjust, record counts, stops and settings, and pass the shift handover to the next operator.

steps.what: Press operator starts machines and runs first pieces
Press operator monitors their operations and adjusts the machine

Press operator records counts, stops and settings: on the shift sheet today; after the change the press control sends counts, stops and settings and the operator checks them and writes the reason for each stop
Press operator writes the shift handover for the next operator

loop.input: The shift's counts, stops and settings from the machine and the operator's short notes.
loop.output: A draft handover in a few sentences.
loop.check: The operator reads the draft against the shift: are the open problems, adjustments and warnings for the next operator right and complete, and does nothing go beyond the record and their notes; code flags any number that differs from the machine record; anything unclear is rewritten by hand.
loop.stop: One draft per shift; a mismatch means the operator writes the handover.
loop.why_not_simpler: The operator's notes are free text that a template cannot fold in.

steps.what: Press operator saves the confirmed handover on the terminal for the next operator

tasks.design: The press control sends counts, stops and settings to the machine terminal ({OPS_SYSTEM}), and the operator only adds reasons for stops. A bounded step drafts the shift handover from the record and the operator's notes; the operator reads it against the shift, corrects it and saves it for the next operator, an ordinary save in the same system. Starting, monitoring and adjusting stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts and stops were written on a paper sheet and compiled in a supervisor's spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Machine controls export counts and states, and language models can draft short handovers.
tasks.still_hard: Older presses without a data link still need manual entry.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing from the sound that the die is starting to wear.
tasks.altitude: The operator adds stop reasons instead of writing all data.

reach.learn: Whether live data replace the supervisor's spreadsheet.

evidence.claim: At Sintex, Factbird read live PLC data on 10 machines, later 30, replacing hand-collected data; efficiency rose 5% in the first week (vendor case).
AI that monitors and evaluates workers is high-risk; plain counting is not AI and the drafting step does not evaluate people.
Machine data tied to an operator login needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from a set-up machine to the shift handover; setup is outside.
Input contract: counts and states from the press control; stop reasons from the operator; fallback is the paper sheet.

Starting, monitoring and adjusting keep their full time. s3 keeps 40 for checking the sent values and writing each stop reason, which stays a first record; s4 keeps 75 because the draft fills numbers and layout and the operator still writes what the next operator must know.
Data are shown per machine and shift.

already_counted.description: Press operator confirms the drafted handover.

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep beyond the steps: entering stop reasons is part of s3, which keeps 40.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of the presses are older ones without a data link, so their sheets are written by hand, and the draft helps little (6.9); high: presses linked and the draft used as designed (14.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study the part and its material, plan the order of cuts, punches and bends, check bend allowances and press force, save the setup sheet and test on a first piece.

steps.what: Press operator studies the part drawing and the physical properties of workpiece materials
Press operator plans sequences of operations for cuts, punches and bends
Press operator looks up bend allowances and press force in tables
Press operator writes the sequence on the setup sheet
Press operator tests the sequence on a first piece

tasks.design: The press control ({OPS_SYSTEM}) computes bend allowances and press force from material, thickness and tooling with standard formulas for the operator to check. Proven sequences are saved with the program in the machine's job library, so a repeat job starts from the last setup. Planning the sequence and testing stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Values were looked up in printed tables and setup sheets kept in binders.
tasks.enabler_now: Press controls compute bend values, and job libraries store proven setups.
tasks.still_hard: New materials and odd shapes still need trial pieces.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a bend order that keeps the flange clear of the tool.

reach.learn: Whether a job library cuts setup time on repeat jobs.

evidence.claim: Press brake controls compute bend allowances and press force with standard formulas.
The Machinery Regulation applies from 20 January 2027 and covers AI-powered safety functions; this design changes no safety function.

assumptions: Boundary: from job specifications to a proven sequence; production runs are outside.
Input contract: material data from the ERP; tooling data set by the process engineer; fallback is printed tables.

Studying, planning and testing keep their full time. s3 keeps 30 for checking the computed values; s4 keeps 50 on the assumption that about half of jobs are repeats that start from the last saved setup, while new jobs are written in full.
research_questions: Does setup time on repeat jobs fall?

incremental.description: Press operator saves proven setups to the job library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few repeat jobs and gaps in the material data, so most sequences are written in full and values still come from tables (10.5); high: half of jobs are repeats and material data are complete (21.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The press operator keeps inspecting, planning sequences and running machines; paper sheets, tables and trips to the office shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An operator who starts each shift with the right job, drawing and setup on screen.

job.title: Cutting, Punching, and Press Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
